sections.h2: What is a small estate affidavit in Texas?
sections.html:
A small estate affidavit is a sworn court filing under Chapter 205 of the Estates Code that lets heirs collect or transfer a modest estate without a full administration. It is meant for people who died without a will and left little behind.

The Texas State Law Library lists it among the informal probate methods, next to the affidavit of heirship and the order of no administration. Because a judge must approve it, it carries more weight with banks and agencies than a sworn statement that is only filed with a clerk. For anyone hoping to sell a Texas house after a death, the first question is whether this tool reaches real estate at all, and the answer is narrow.

sections.h2: What are the requirements for a Texas small estate affidavit?
sections.html:
The estate must have no will, no pending application for administration, and countable assets of $75,000 or less. The $75,000 figure leaves out the homestead and exempt property.

The State Law Library guide adds that the estate needs enough assets to pay its debts and that all the heirs must agree. The county clerk manual describes further mechanics: the affidavit is sworn by two disinterested witnesses, at least 30 days must have passed since the death, and no petition for a personal representative can be pending or already granted.

  • The person died intestate, meaning without a will.
  • Assets total $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead or exempt property.
  • No application for administration has been filed.
  • The estate can pay its debts.
  • Every heir agrees to the affidavit.
  • The court approves it.

sections.h2: Can a small estate affidavit be used to sell a house in Texas?
sections.html:
Generally no. The guide states that the estate cannot include real property, with one exception: a homestead that passes to the surviving spouse or minor children.

When that exception applies, a copy of the approved affidavit is recorded with the county clerk in the county where the homestead sits. That recorded copy is what a buyer's title company will look for. An heir who inherits an ordinary rental house, a vacant lot or a second property needs a different route, which is covered below.

If you are in a hurry to close, speak with the title company before you sign anything. They decide which recorded documents they will insure, and that can differ from what a family expects.

sections.h2: What other ways exist to transfer inherited Texas real estate?
sections.html:
The right document depends on whether there is a will, whether the estate was administered, and whether the owner signed a transfer on death deed. The State Law Library's property deeds page pairs each situation with the paperwork to record.

Recorded paperwork by situation, per Texas State Law Library guidance
SituationWhat gets recorded
Transfer on death deed in placeAffidavit of death and the death certificate
Estate administered by a personal representativeExecutor's or administrator's deed
Will with no debts besides real estate liens (muniment of title)Court order and the will
OtherwiseAffidavit of heirship

Source: Texas State Law Library, Probate: Property Deeds.

Note that the county cannot simply add heirs to the old deed. A new instrument has to be recorded.

sections.h2: How is an affidavit of heirship different?
sections.html:
An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement of who the heirs are, filed with the county clerk without any judge reviewing it. No law forces a buyer, bank or title insurer to accept it.

That makes it a weaker tool than a small estate affidavit even when it is easier to file. A determination of heirship and an order of no administration are the other routes the guide names when a title company wants court backing. If the family expects to sell soon, ask the buyer's title company early which one they will accept.

sections.h2: How long do heirs have to probate a will in Texas?
sections.html:
A will generally has to be offered for probate within four years of the death, although a court may accept a later filing for an acceptable reason. The application goes to the probate court, usually in the county where the person lived.

A valid will is written, signed and witnessed by two people, while a holographic will needs no witnesses. When there is a will and the only debts are liens on real estate, a muniment of title can transfer property without administration. The court order and the will are then filed with the county clerk where the land is located.

sections.h2: Where do you file in Texas, and what does the clerk do?
sections.html:
Probate filings, including applications and small estate affidavits, go through the county clerk, who also records deeds and notices. The clerk is the county recorder, which is why recorded transfer paperwork ends up there too.

  • Small estate affidavits and probate applications: file in the county probate court, typically where the decedent lived.
  • Homestead copies of an approved affidavit: record with the county clerk where the property is.
  • Deeds, orders and affidavits of heirship: record in the county where the real property sits.

A conveyance of real property can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged before an officer authorized to take acknowledgments or sworn before two subscribing witnesses. The clerk manual lists the current fee structure, so ask the clerk for the total before you go.

sections.h2: What happens to an inherited homestead's property tax exemption?
sections.html:
Heirs who are not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the prior owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation to claim the homestead exemption. The Comptroller lists those items on its exemptions page.

The exemption matters for a sale because a buyer who acquires the home after January 1 may get the exemption for the rest of that tax year right away if the previous owner did not receive it. School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and an owner who is 65 or older or disabled gets an additional $60,000 from school districts. A surviving spouse age 55 or older may keep the deceased spouse's 65-or-older exemption in certain cases.

sections.h2: Can a transfer on death deed avoid the whole process?
sections.html:
It can, if the owner signed and recorded it before death. A transfer on death deed passes real property without probate, can name charities as beneficiaries, and can be cancelled by the owner.

It must be recorded before the owner's death in the county where the property sits. The Lady Bird deed, also called an enhanced life estate deed, lets the owner sell or mortgage the property without the beneficiary's consent, though the State Law Library notes that there is no official form. Families who learn that an older relative signed one should locate the recorded copy at the county clerk's office before anything else.

Where no such deed exists and the estate does not qualify for the small estate route, a family can still sell after a court order, an executor's deed or another recorded instrument supports the title. Plan for the time those steps take before you accept a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the dollar limit for a Texas small estate affidavit?
faqs.a: $75,000 in assets, not counting the homestead or exempt property. The estate must also be able to pay its debts, and all heirs must agree.

faqs.q: Does a small estate affidavit work if there is a will?
faqs.a: No. The procedure is for estates without a will. With a will, the usual options are probate or a muniment of title, which the court approves.

faqs.q: Can I sell inherited land using a small estate affidavit?
faqs.a: Usually not. The affidavit cannot cover real property other than a homestead passing to a spouse or minor children, so other heirs typically need probate, a recorded deed or another court-backed route.

faqs.q: How long after death can the affidavit be filed?
faqs.a: At least 30 days must pass after the death before the affidavit is made, according to the county clerk manual. Ask the probate court clerk about any other timing the court applies.

faqs.q: Will a title company accept an affidavit of heirship?
faqs.a: Not automatically. No law forces anyone to accept it, so confirm with the title company before you list the house.
